title: Effector-host interactome map links type III secretion systems in healthy gut microbiomes to immune modulation.
authors: Young, Veronika; Dohai, Bushra; Halder, Hridi; Fernandez-Macgregor, Jaime; van Heusden, Niels S; Hitch, Thomas C A; Weller, Benjamin; Hyden, Patrick; Saha, Deeya; Pieren, Daan K J; Rittchen, Sonja; Lambourne, Luke; Maseko, Sibusiso B; Lin, Chung-Wen; Tun, Ye Min; Bibus, Jonas; Pletschacher, Luisa; Boujeant, Megane; Choteau, Sebastien A; Bergogne, Lou; Perrin, Jeremie; Ober, Franziska; Schwehn, Patrick; Rothballer, Simin T; Altmann, Melina; Altmann, Stefan; Strobel, Alexandra; Rothballer, Michael; Tofaute, Marie; Kotlarz, Daniel; Heinig, Matthias; Clavel, Thomas; Calderwood, Michael A; Vidal, Marc; Twizere, Jean-Claude; Vincentelli, Renaud; Krappmann, Daniel; Boes, Marianne; Falter, Claudia; Rattei, Thomas; Brun, Christine; Zanzoni, Andreas; Falter-Braun, Pascal
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过机器学习预测肠道菌群T3SS效应蛋白并构建效应蛋白-宿主蛋白互作图，虽涉及蛋白互作但非蛋白质-DNA体系，且无结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联度低。
abstract: Pseudomonadota (formerly Proteobacteria) are prevalent in the commensal human gut microbiota, but also include many pathogens that rely on secretion systems to support pathogenicity by injecting proteins into host cells. Here we show that 80% of Pseudomonadota from healthy gut microbiomes also have intact type III secretion systems (T3SS). Candidate effectors predicted by machine learning display sequence and structural features that are distinct from those of pathogen effectors. Towards a systems-level functional understanding, we experimentally constructed a protein-protein meta-interactome map between human proteins and commensal effectors. Network analyses uncovered that effector-targeted neighbourhoods are enriched for genetic variation linked to microbiome-associated conditions, including autoimmune and metabolic diseases. Metagenomic analysis revealed effector enrichment in Crohn's disease but depletion in ulcerative colitis. Functionally, commensal effectors can translocate into human cells and modulate NF-kappaB signalling and cytokine secretion in vitro. Our findings indicate that T3SS contribute to microorganism-host cohabitation and that effector-host protein interactions may represent an underappreciated route by which commensal gut microbiota influences health.
abstract_zh: 假单胞菌门（Pseudomonadota，原变形菌门）在人类共生肠道微生物群中普遍存在，但也包含许多依赖分泌系统通过向宿主细胞注入蛋白质来支持致病性的病原体。在此，我们表明来自健康肠道微生物组的80%的假单胞菌门也具有完整的III型分泌系统（T3SS）。通过机器学习预测的候选效应子显示出与病原体效应子不同的序列和结构特征。为了在系统层面进行功能理解，我们实验构建了人类蛋白质与共生效应子之间的蛋白质-蛋白质元相互作用图谱。网络分析揭示，效应子靶向的邻域富集了与微生物组相关疾病（包括自身免疫和代谢疾病）相关的遗传变异。宏基因组分析显示，效应子在克罗恩病中富集，但在溃疡性结肠炎中减少。在功能上，共生效应子可以转位进入人类细胞，并在体外调节NF-kappaB信号传导和细胞因子分泌。我们的发现表明，T3SS有助于微生物与宿主的共居，且效应子-宿主蛋白质相互作用可能代表了共生肠道微生物群影响健康的一条被低估的途径。
